title: The Control Language
intro: Inside .control ... .endc (or at the ngspice prompt) you write scripts in ngspice's own language, inherited from SPICE3's nutmeg. It has two kinds of data, vectors and variables, a handful of control structures, and about a hundred commands. It is small and a little quirky, but enough to automate almost any simulation task.

blocks.text: Every analysis creates a plot: a named set of vectors (op1, dc1, ac1, tran1, noise1 ...). Vectors are arrays of real or complex numbers with a type (voltage, current, time, frequency ...); one of them is the scale (time, frequency, the swept source). let creates or changes vectors; the newest plot is the current one, and setplot switches between them. Vectors in other plots are reached as plotname.vector, and the const plot holds constants: pi, e, c, kelvin, echarge, boltz, planck, yes, no, true, false.

blocks.source:
Vectors, plots and expressions
V1 in 0 SIN(0 1 1k)
R1 in out 1k
C1 out 0 100n
.control
  tran 10u 3m
  let p = v(out)*i(V1)              $ element-wise: instantaneous power
  let vpk = vecmax(v(out))          $ a one-element vector
  let n = length(time)
  let first = v(out)[0]              $ index from 0
  let some = v(out)[10,20]           $ a range
  print vpk n first
  let w = vector(5)                  $ [0 1 2 3 4]
  compose z values 1 2 4             $ a vector from listed values
  let z = z * 2
  print w z
  setplot const
  print pi boltz
  setplot tran1
  print mean(p) tran1.vpk
.endc
.end

items: Arithmetic is element by element; a scalar combines with every element. Vectors of different lengths are cut to the shorter one, with a warning.

Functions: mag, ph, cph, unwrap, real, imag, db, j, conj, abs, sqrt, exp, ln, log (both natural), log10, sin ... atanh, floor, ceil, norm, mean, avg (running average), stddev, integ, deriv, group_delay, vecmin, vecmax, minimum, maximum, length, vector, unitvec, interpolate, fft, ifft, sortorder, m3avg, mtimeavg, and random functions rnd, sgauss, sunif, poisson, exponential.
Comparison and logic (eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le, and, or, not, or the symbols) give 1 or 0, element by element.
v(a,b) is v(a) - v(b); i(V1) is the current of V1; @dev[param] reads device data; quoted names reach odd characters: let x = \"v(n-1)\".
setscale changes a plot's scale vector, so plot v(out) vs v(in) or setscale v(in) plots against another vector.
destroy removes plots to free memory in long loops; remzerovec removes empty vectors.

blocks.text: Variables are separate from vectors: strings, numbers, booleans or lists, set with set and read with \$name. They control options (set units=degrees, set filetype=ascii, set wr_vecnames) and hold strings for scripts. \$&vector turns a vector's first value into text, so you can print a vector inside an echo or build a file name. Lists are written in parentheses.

blocks.source:
Variables, strings and the conversion between them
V1 a 0 1.5
R1 a 0 1k
.control
  set name = "run1"
  set vals = ( 1 2.5 4 )
  set flag
  op
  let ia = -i(V1)*1000
  echo "the current in $name is $&ia mA"
  if $?flag
    echo "flag is set"
  end
  echo "second value: $vals[2], count: $#vals"
  set outfile = "{$name}.txt"        $ braces end the name: $name.txt would look up "name.txt"
  echo "would write to $outfile"
  strcmp res "$name" "run1"
  echo "strcmp gives $res"
.endc
.end

items: \$name: the value; \$?name: 1 if set, else 0; \$#name: the number of words in a list; \$name[2]: an element of a list (from 1).
\$&vec: the value of a vector, \$&vec[3] an element. Needed wherever a command expects text, such as alter, echo, file names and if with variables.
A dot is a legal character in a variable name, so \$name.txt looks for a variable called name.txt. Write {\$name}.txt to end the name.
Strings: strcmp, strstr, strslice, and setcs to keep upper case. -D name=value on the command line sets a variable before the script runs.

Predefined variables include curplot, curplottitle, plots, temp, tnom, and many that change behaviour: units, filetype, width, height, nfreqs, specwindow, wr_singlescale, wr_vecnames, noaskquit, num_threads, sourcepath, interactive, ngbehavior.

blocks.source:
Control structures
V1 a 0 1
R1 a b 1k
R2 b 0 1k
.control
  foreach r 1k 2k 5k 10k
    alter R2 $r
    op
    echo "R2 = $r: v(b) = $&v(b)"
  end
  let k = 0
  repeat 3
    let k = k + 1
  end
  while k < 10
    let k = k * 2
  end
  dowhile k > 1
    let k = k - 5
  end
  if k < 0
    echo "k went negative: $&k"
  else
    echo "k is $&k"
  end
.endc
.end

blocks.text: foreach var values ... end loops over words (numbers or names); repeat N ... end, while cond ... end, dowhile cond ... end, if cond ... else ... end, break and continue, and label/goto. Conditions are vector expressions; an empty or zero result is false. Each block must close with its own end.
Changing the circuit and running again

items: alter R1 2k, alter R1 resistance = 2k, alter @R1[resistance] = 2k: change an instance parameter. alter @V1[pulse] = [ 0 1 0 1n 1n 5n 10n ] changes a vector parameter. alter @m1[w] = 2u changes a transistor's width.
altermod nch vth0 = 0.5 (or altermod @nch[vth0] = 0.5) changes a model parameter for every device using it; altermod nch file new.mod replaces a whole model from a file.
alterparam name = value then reset: change a .param and re-expand the netlist, so every expression using it is recomputed.
reset: re-read the stored netlist, undoing alters and drawing new random parameter values.
option name=value (or .options in the netlist) changes simulator options between runs: option reltol=1e-4, option method=gear, option temp=85.

source file reads another netlist or script; remcirc removes the current circuit; setcirc switches between loaded circuits; mc_source reloads the netlist from its stored copy (Monte Carlo with new random values per run).
shell runs an operating-system command; cd, getcwd; fopen, fread, fclose read text files into variables.
define f(x) expr: a user function for vector expressions.

blocks.text: Running commands before the circuit is parsed

Commands in a .control block normally run after the circuit is read. Some must run before: loading code models or .osdi files, or setting variables that change how the netlist is read. Prefix them with pre_ (pre_osdi file.osdi, pre_set ...), or put them in .spiceinit.

blocks.title: Echo a vector
blocks.text: Why does echo \"gain is gain\" not print the number, and how do you fix it?
solution: echo prints text; gain there is just a word. Use \$&gain to substitute the vector's value: echo \"gain is \$&gain\".

blocks.title: Sweep a capacitor
blocks.text: Write a loop that runs a transient for C1 = 1p, 2p, 5p and prints the delay each time (measured by meas tran td trig ... targ ...).
solution:
foreach c 1p 2p 5p
  alter C1 \$c
  tran 1p 2n
  meas tran td trig v(in) val=0.5 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0.5 fall=1
  echo \"C1=\$c delay=\$&td\"
end
blocks.answer: foreach with alter, tran, meas and echo.

items: H. Vogt, G. Atkinson, D. Warning and P. Nenzi, Ngspice User's Manual, version 47, 2026 (ngspice.sourceforge.io/docs.html), chapter 13 (interactive interpreter: expressions, plots, commands, control structures, variables, scripts).
